item.content:encoded:
The review covered the Vodafone Vanua and Royal Tea Ranadi provincial competitions, including Northern Bulls, Ovalau, Namosi, Serua and Nasinu, as well as the Vodafone Deans, Weet-Bix Raluve and Vodafone Juniors competitions.

FRU says the session brought together key stakeholders to assess the 2026 season, identify key strengths and challenges, capture lessons learned, and set priorities for improving the delivery of competitions in 2027.

They say the session also examined financial acquittals from the Schools Rugby, Vanua and Ranadi treasurers, reinforcing Fiji Rakavi’s commitment to sound financial management, transparency and accountability across the game.

The review process provides an important opportunity to assess how competitions were delivered, identify operational and administrative gaps, capture stakeholder feedback, and apply lessons from the 2026 season to strengthen planning and delivery for 2027.

The next review will be held in the Northern Division next week, followed by the Western Division the following week.

FRU says the Skipper Cup and Marama Championship will be reviewed separately at the conclusion of their respective competitions.

They say as Fiji Rakavi looks towards 2027, the focus remains on strengthening governance, improving competition delivery, and building a sustainable rugby pathway from grassroots and schools through to provincial and national representation.

item.title: Fiji Kulas hunt for first win against Vanuatu tonight
item.description: The Fiji Kulas will be hunting for their first win of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 when they take on Vanuatu at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva tonight. The Kulas will be looking to bounce back after going down 4-0 to Papua New Guinea in their opening match.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Kulas will be hunting for their first win of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 when they take on Vanuatu at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva tonight.

The Kulas will be looking to bounce back after going down 4-0 to Papua New Guinea in their opening match.

Vanuatu, meanwhile, started their campaign with a 1-all draw against the Solomon Islands.

The women’s competition continues at 4pm today with New Caledonia taking on Papua New Guinea before Fiji faces Vanuatu at 7pm.

Meanwhile, in the men’s competition, Papua New Guinea beat Vanuatu 2-1 on Friday, while the Bula Boys were held to a thrilling 3-all draw by the Solomon Islands.

The men’s competition continues tomorrow with New Caledonia taking on the Solomon Islands at 4pm, before the Bula Boys face Vanuatu at 7pm.

item.title: Fijiana thump Hong Kong China 54-26
item.description: Adi Salote Nailolo opened the scoring in the eighth minute after Fijiana dominated the opening exchanges. Varanisese Qoro then extended Fiji’s lead three minutes later, chasing in from halfway to put the finishing touch on a flowing broken-play move featuring excellent link-up and wraparound skills.
item.content:encoded:
Adi Salote Nailolo opened the scoring in the eighth minute after Fijiana dominated the opening exchanges.

Varanisese Qoro then extended Fiji’s lead three minutes later, chasing in from halfway to put the finishing touch on a flowing broken-play move featuring excellent link-up and wraparound skills.

Tanya Dhar and Sabay Lynam then scored for Hong Kong China to briefly put their side ahead as they dominated for 10 minutes midway through the first half, in a match between the two comeback sides from the opening weekend.

Qoro scored her second try shortly after the restart, slicing through the narrowest of gaps in the Hong Kong China defensive line as Fiji increased the attacking pressure.

Player of the match Atelaite Buna Ralivanawa and Merewairita Neivosa combined to score three more tries in the six minutes before half-time.

Ralivanawa’s first try of the two was particularly impressive, as she twice stayed in play near the touchline while holding off defenders to cross the line.

Neivosa’s try was a fine example of effective, high-speed link play.

Fiji could have taken their foot off the gas, but replacement Zipporah Sorokacika crashed over for Fiji’s seventh try just moments after coming on, 11 minutes into the second half.

Fiji extended their lead again 13 minutes from time when another replacement, Vasemaca Duva, accelerated on to the ball and raced untouched through the defence to score Fiji’s eighth and final try of the match.

Fijiana take on the Netherlands on Saturday at 4pm in Hong Kong.

item.title: Fiji goes down 20-15 to Japan in PNC final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 20/09/2026 Conceding too many penalties proved too costly for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as they went down 20-15 to Japan in the 2026 Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 20/09/2026

Conceding too many penalties proved too costly for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as they went down 20-15 to Japan in the 2026 Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo.

This was the third consecutive time the two teams had met in the final.

Fiji conceded 14 penalties, where Japan had only 5.

The final did not disappoint, with the match going down to the wire.

The game was filled with intensity as both teams hunted for the win.

Virimi Vakatawa scored the first try of the match, putting Fiji 7-3 ahead, but Japan responded with a try from Mamoru Harada to take a 10-7 lead.

Captain Tevita Ikanivere then crossed the try line in the 26th minute to put the Fijians back in front, 12-10.

Fiji continued to commit mistakes, giving Japan plenty of possession, but they held their line to take a 12-10 lead into halftime.

The second half was played with the same intensity as the Japanese side brought their A-game, putting pressure on the Fijians and disrupting their game plan.

Japan managed to score two more tries in the second half through Ben Gunter and Samisoni Tua to put the Fijians on the back foot.

The final five minutes saw both teams produce some spectacular rugby, but in the end, Japan’s defence stood tall to secure the victory.

item.title: Pearls finish on a high, but World Cup dream ends in Tonga
item.description: Fiji produced one of its strongest performances of the tournament, taking control early and heading into half-time with a commanding 32–16 lead. The Pearls maintained their composure after the break, continuing to apply pressure and eventually sealing a 21-goal victory.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji produced one of its strongest performances of the tournament, taking control early and heading into half-time with a commanding 32–16 lead.

The Pearls maintained their composure after the break, continuing to apply pressure and eventually sealing a 21-goal victory.

The result provided a positive finish to Fiji’s campaign, but it was not enough to keep their Netball World Cup hopes alive.

Tonga and Samoa secured the two qualifying places from the Oceania region and will now turn their attention to the Netball World Cup in Australia in 2027.

For the Pearls, the road to the next major tournament begins again from here.

item.title: Nadroga end Nadi’s unbeaten run in Skipper Cup thriller
item.description: The highly anticipated Western derby lived up to expectations as the two sides battled through an intense and physical 80 minutes. Nadroga opened the scoring in the 18th minute after Nadi lost possession while on attack.
item.content:encoded:
The highly anticipated Western derby lived up to expectations as the two sides battled through an intense and physical 80 minutes.

Nadroga opened the scoring in the 18th minute after Nadi lost possession while on attack.

The Stallions quickly turned defence into attack, with centre Kavekini Boselawa finishing off the counter-attack to give the visitors an early 5–0 lead.

Nadi responded through flanker Peni Vukivuki, bringing the home side back into the contest.

Nadroga, however, regained the advantage when full-back Sefanaia Tokaduadua crossed the try line, giving the visitors a 10–7 lead at half-time.

Tight-head prop Josh Uluibau powered his way over the line in the 62nd minute, sending the home crowd into celebration as Nadi moved ahead 14–10.

Both sides then exchanged penalties as the pressure continued to build.

With the match entering its final stages, Nadroga were dealt another setback when they were reduced to 14 men after receiving a red card.

Their persistence was eventually rewarded when replacement hooker Apenisa Lanivia crashed over the try line to score the winning try.

The late effort secured a dramatic 20–17 victory for Nadroga and brought Nadi’s unbeaten run to an end.

item.title: 20-year-old Ba defender Isimeli Gavidi earns first Bula Boys cap
item.description: At just 20, Ba defender Isimeli Gavidi has earned his first senior international cap after being handed a starting role for the Bula Boys against Solomon Islands in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup. The Ba defender started for Fiji in their opening match of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup against Solomon Islands at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on Friday night.
item.content:encoded:
At just 20, Ba defender Isimeli Gavidi has earned his first senior international cap after being handed a starting role for the Bula Boys against Solomon Islands in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup.

The Ba defender started for Fiji in their opening match of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup against Solomon Islands at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on Friday night.

Gavidi’s debut comes after progressing through Fiji’s age-group teams before establishing himself at domestic level with Ba.

The young defender shared the field with experienced internationals, including captain Roy Krishna, as Fiji and Solomon Islands played out an entertaining 3-all draw.

The appearance marks Gavidi’s first senior international cap and gives him an opportunity to build on his progress as he looks to establish himself in the Bula Boys squad.
